rpc: Phase 2 SSE push (issue #15 Tier 2) — push nudges, walletd consumes, UIs render <RTT
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/25

Issue #15 Tier 2, Route A (per-script subscription routing). The node pushes a nudge the moment a subscribed script's mempool/confirmed state changes, so a wallet renders the update at network-RTT instead of waiting for its next poll.

**Already shipping in production.** Deployed on two nodes, and consumed by the released wallets: [exfer-walletd v1.11.2](https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-walletd/releases/tag/v1.11.2), embedded in [exfer-walletd-desktop v0.13.1](https://github.com/exfer-stack/exfer-walletd-desktop/releases/tag/v0.13.1) and [exfer-walletd-mobile v0.5.4](https://github.com/exfer-stack/get/releases/tag/mobile-v0.5.4). Not a proposal — the code those builds talk to.

## Commits

1. `events: per-script EventBus` — `HashMap<ScriptKey, HashSet<SubscriberId>>` routing so emit is O(subscribers for that script), not O(all connections). Bounded per-sub mpsc; on overflow the sub is flagged lagged and the next send is preceded by a `Resync`. No new deps.
2. `mempool, sync: wire EventBus through admit / remove / commit` — `Mempool::set_event_bus()`; `index_entry`/`deindex_entry` emit per touched script (covers admit/remove/evict/revalidate/confirm); block commit emits per output script. `Node` gains `pub event_bus`.
3. `rpc_sse: long-lived SSE endpoint` — `text/event-stream`, events `script_changed` / `tip` / `resync`, subscribe via `?addresses=<hex>,...`, snapshot-then-stream, 25s heartbeat, separate connection pool, per-IP + per-conn caps. SSE permits don't touch the JSON-RPC pool.
4. `rpc: production-harden SSE for direct (non-fly) deployment` — nodes run direct on Vultr now, not behind a fly.io L7 edge: drop the PROXY-protocol strip and `POST /sse` (fly workarounds) → native `GET /sse` only; raise caps (per-IP 4→64, total 256→2048) for CGNAT-shared mobile IPs; TCP keepalive (socket2) frees a silently-dropped client's slot in ~120s; detach the SSE handler from the 30s per-request timeout (it was tearing every stream down at ~30s).
5. `events: make tip an opt-in SSE event` — `emit_tip_changed` used to wake EVERY subscriber on every block; a per-address subscriber that re-pulls on each wake blew the node's 30 balance/utxo-queries-per-minute cap (sends then failed "network busy"). Tip is now opt-in (`subscribe(scripts, wants_tip)`, default off, SSE `?tips=1`). Confirmations still arrive as `script_changed`, so script subscribers lose nothing.

`cargo test --lib` green; tests cover the bus (route/dedup/lagged-resync/unsubscribe), the mempool emit path, SSE query parsing + per-IP cap, and the new tip opt-in.

## Measured end-to-end latency ("B sees A's pending tx in the UI")
Scales with B↔node RTT: same-region ~50ms, one transcontinental hop ~250ms, two hops ~600ms. Versus the old 4–18s poll, the difference between "is it stuck?" and "instant". Poll fallback is automatic when a node doesn't speak `/sse`.
